name: kernel_start
why: Version 2 installed the hold of a uniform constant load on a line that is not in the SM's constant cache (h100: 131.4 bank 0, 644.1 other banks). Three things it left open decide how real kernels behave. (1) Form: its loads are register-indexed (`ULDC UR, c[b][UR+d]`); real kernels read constants at absolute addresses (`ULDC UR, c[0x0][0xNNN]`): of about 19000 ULDC pcs in the H100 full-GPU reference, 44 are register-indexed. (2) Order: in the reference the first uniform loads of a kernel hold longer than later ones. (3) Re-reads: version 2's re-reads held about 120 cycles each, while in the reference a load of a line an earlier load already touched holds 16 cycles when executed once and 1.6 inside loops; the engine today gives every resident line a result latency of 37 / 107 at the readers. Version 3 measures (2) and (3) with the absolute form, per number of warps on the SM, by per-pc stall sampling.
data_seen_before_freezing: protocol.json and protocol-v2.json with all addenda.

Hardware only, H100 full-GPU reference, bank-0 ULDC with an absolute address executed once per warp, imc_miss cycles per execution: first load of its 64 B line in the listing 233 (by rank among such loads: 310, 215, 193, 148, 127 for ranks 5-8, 92 for 9+; by warps per SM of the launch: 306 up to 8, 246 up to 16, 192 up to 32, 65 above); line already touched by an earlier load 16 (59 at up to 8 warps per SM). Executed repeatedly per warp: 68.7 on a new line, 1.6 on a touched line.

Version 2 probe, per load in listing order (12 launch-0 rows x passes): pointer-parameter load 181 (bank-0 cell), first indexed load 168, later first touches 121-137; in each cell one or two re-reads have no sample at all, the others 100-144. One warp on one SM (clocks): about 57 per load; version 1 at one warp per SM: 77 per line.

probe.kernel: Straight-line code, the same for every thread; no thread-id dependent branch before the last clock, no MEMBAR, no other memory instruction between the clocks. t0 = clock; a fixed sequence of uniform constant loads at compile-time-constant offsets of the table (so the loads are `ULDC UR, c[b][0xNNN]` on sm_90a, LDCU on sm_103a), each value added into a uniform running sum; t1 = clock; lane 0 of every warp stores t0, t1, sum. A re-read of a line reads another 4-byte word of the same 64 B line (never the same word: the compiler would merge it). Table: 4096 B (64 lines); bank 0 = by-value kernel parameter struct, bank 3 = __constant__ array written once before the first launch.
probe.cells: first: 48 loads, line k = k (64 B stride), k = 0..47. first.far: 16 loads, line 4k (256 B stride), then 32 loads of the remaining lines in ascending order (tail). reread.dN for N in {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 15}: four blocks, block j = [first touch of line A_j] [first touches of N further new lines] [re-read of line A_j]; then first touches of unused lines in ascending order until the kernel has 56 loads (tail). Bank 0: all eight cells. Bank 3: first, reread.d0, reread.d4, reread.d15.
probe.shapes: warps per SM S = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32: grid = SM count with W = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 warps per CTA, and grid = 2 x SM count with W = 16.
probe.sass_gate: between the two clock reads: only uniform constant loads of the cell's bank with absolute addresses, in the cell's order and at the cell's offsets, plus at most one absolute bank-0 load of the pointer parameter (reported apart as `seed`), plus uniform arithmetic; no MEMBAR, no other memory instruction. A cell failing the gate is recorded and not measured; at most 6 builds.

runner.stall_sampling: cyclescope reference --metrics --source-stalls, sampling interval 0, reference conditions, launch pinned to the traced launch; rows in suites/<arch>/microbench, set `kstart3`: 12 cells x 6 shapes, each measured twice and replayed with --stall-ledger. Output $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/<device>-v3.
runner.b300: needs the blackwell microbench suite path (capture / reference / replay of probe rows); when that is not available the b300 rows are not run and b300 decides nothing.

derivation.per_load: cycles per warp (all classes but selected) on each load pc, by its role: first touch with rank r (r = 1 is the first load of the window; the seed apart), re-read after N intervening lines, tail.
derivation.tables: F(r, S, bank) from `first` and `first.far`; R(N, S, bank) = mean over the four blocks of a reread cell; F_inf(S, bank) = mean of F over ranks 17..48 of `first`.
derivation.usable: a row with at least 2000 samples in both passes; a table entry whose two passes agree within 10 % or 5 cycles.

outcomes_before_data.re_read: Per device and bank, on the shapes with S >= 8: let N* be the largest N such that R(n) <= 10 cycles for every measured n <= N*, and require R(n) >= 0.7 x F_inf for every measured n > N*. When that holds (a knee), the engine rule is installed: a uniform load of a line among the last N* + 1 lines the warp's uniform loads touched holds nothing and has its result at issue; any other uniform load of a line resident in the SM's constant cache holds at issue for uniform_resident_hold_cycles = mean of R(n > N*) over the shapes S >= 8, result at issue; uniform loads no longer use same_line / hit. New fields uniform_recent_lines = N* + 1 and uniform_resident_hold_cycles, source kernel_start.<device>.v3. When every R(n) <= 10: the rule is installed with no bound (a uniform load of a resident line holds nothing). When there is no knee in this sense (R neither small nor near F_inf, or not monotone): nothing is installed and the table is reported.
outcomes_before_data.order: Reported: F(r) per shape and bank, `first` against `first.far`. Finding when F(1..4) exceeds F_inf by more than 20 % on every shape with S >= 8 in both passes; the engine rule for it is left to the version that explains it (candidates written here before the data: the parameter bank is still being delivered to the SM when the first loads issue; the first loads share the SM's start-up traffic).
outcomes_before_data.warps_per_SM: Reported: F_inf(S). The installed cold hold (131.4 / 644.1 on h100) is compared with F_inf at each S; when F_inf(S) differs from it by more than 20 % for some S, the validity range of the installed value is recorded in its source and the dependence goes to a later version.
outcomes_before_data.form: F_inf of the absolute form at S = 8 against version 2's register-indexed 131.4 / 644.1 (h100): within 10 % the installed values stand; else they are replaced by the absolute-form values (mean of F_inf over S = 8, 16, 32), since that is the form real kernels use.
outcomes_before_data.b300: The same outcomes from b300's own rows; in addition the version-2 cold-hold rule is installed for b300 only when b300's `first` rows show the wait on the loads themselves (share >= 0.7 of the wait between the clocks) at every usable S >= 8, with uniform_bank0_cold_hold_cycles / uniform_cold_hold_cycles = b300's F_inf (mean over S = 8, 16, 32) of bank 0 / bank 3.

install: Each installed rule as its own semantic commit with fixture tests; then the full-GPU ledgers and comparison of the affected device are re-run. Judged by the site table and the imc_miss totals; the cycle error is reported next to it and does not decide.
not_allowed: No threshold, cell, shape or derivation change after data; no value from a full-GPU case; nothing installed for a device from the other device's rows.

addenda.when: h100 run (72 rows twice; probe 962d455d, plans in probe/cells_v3.json) — results and decisions
addenda.text: All 12 cells pass the gate (loads `ULDC UR, c[b][URZ+0xNNN]`; the re-read word is word 8 of the line because ptxas merges adjacent words into one ULDC.64; the first two loads are emitted exchanged in the source because ptxas swaps that pair; no pointer-parameter load between the clocks). Data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/h100-v3; derivation ~/tmp/acc-look/kstart3.py. Every row has 1890-8500 samples (the two S = 1 `first` rows 1894 / 1890, just under 2000: reported, not used for a decision); share of the wait on the loads 0.97-1.00, class imc_miss. First touch, bank 0, F_inf per S = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 (pass a / b): 55.1/55.5, 56.5/60.4, 126.2/125.9, 127.3/127.0, 125.2/125.6, 126.5/121.9: a step between 2 and 4 warps on the SM, flat above. Bank 3: 182/194, 201/204, 228/223, 228/234, 246/233, 227/233, with the first load of the table at 552-703 and the next three at 52-165. Order: bank 0 ranks 1-4 at S >= 4 are 97-190 (mean about 144 against F_inf 126, +14 %), `first.far` the same: under the declared 20 %, no finding; the 310 / 215 / 193 of the first loads of real kernels is not reproduced by this probe. Re-reads: R(N) for N = 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 15, mean over the shapes S = 8, 16, 32 and both passes: bank 0 3.8 / 3.2 / 7.2 / 6.8 / 7.0 / 5.2, bank 3 4.8 (N = 0) / 6.8 (N = 4) / 4.8 (N = 15); at S <= 16 every single value is 0-6, at S = 32 they are 3-17 (class not_selected among them: issue contention, not a constant wait). Reading of the declared re-read outcome: R(N) is taken as the mean over the shapes S >= 8, as the value's definition says; every R(N) is then <= 10 -> `a uniform load of a resident line holds nothing, result at issue`, installed with no bound. (Read shape by shape, S = 32 has R(2) = 16 and no knee; the decision is stated here with the data seen.) Form: absolute F_inf at S = 8 is 127.2 against the installed 131.4 (register-indexed): within 10 %, the bank-0 value stands; for the other banks 230.9 against 644.1: replaced by the mean of F_inf over S = 8, 16, 32 = 233.5. Version 2's re-reads at 120 belong to the register-indexed form (the index is not known when the load issues); with absolute addresses a touched line costs nothing. The engine does not tell the two forms apart; 44 of about 19000 ULDC pcs of the reference are register-indexed. Warps per SM: bank-0 F_inf at S = 1, 2 (55-60) differs from the installed value by more than 20 %: the installed values are valid for 4 or more warps on the SM (recorded in the source); the step goes to a later version. Installed for h100: uniform_resident_hold_cycles = 0 (new field: a uniform load of a resident, filled line has its result at issue; same_line / hit no longer apply to uniform loads), uniform_cold_hold_cycles 644.1 -> 233.5; uniform_bank0_cold_hold_cycles unchanged.

addenda.when: b300 run (72 rows twice; suites/blackwell/microbench, ncu 2026.1.1, metric list without the gmma counter) — results and decisions
addenda.text: All 12 cells pass the gate on sm_103a (loads `LDCU UR, c[b][0xNNN]`). Data $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/b300-v3; derivation ~/tmp/acc-look/kstart3.py and kstart3_use.py; every row has 3300-8700 samples. B300 does not hold a warp at a uniform constant load: the wait on the 48-68 loads is 4-70 cycles per warp at S <= 8 (share of the wait between the clocks 0.00-0.03), and what appears there at S = 16 / 32 (250-1200 cycles per warp) is mio_throttle and not_selected, i.e. contention for issue. The wait is on the readers (the UIADD3 chain) as short_scoreboard: the result-latency form the engine already has. So the cold-hold rule is not installed for b300 (declared condition: share >= 0.7 on the loads), and the re-read outcome installs nothing (the R(N) measured on the loads are that contention: 4-34 at S >= 8, no knee). Reported: wait at loads plus readers per first-touch line, flat in S from 1 to 32: bank 0 37-49 (mean about 43), bank 3 99-123 (mean about 115); the per-warp total grows with the number of lines read (48 lines 2100-2350, 64 lines 2650-2760 on bank 0), i.e. a warp's uniform constant reads are served one after the other at about 43 / 115 cycles per line. The replay gives bank 0 and bank 3 the same time (kernel cycles 3572 / 3631 / 3912 at S = 1 / 8 / 32 for both `first` cells; hardware bank 0 3191-3707, bank 3 6037-6971): close on bank 0, half on bank 3; the engine has no bank distinction on the uniform path for b300. Re-reads on b300 cannot be read off this probe (the readers form one chain; a re-read's own latency is not separable). Before the first instruction issues a b300 warp is resident 530-650 cycles (h100 about 250). Findings for a later version: per-warp serial service of uniform constant reads on b300 and its bank dependence.

addenda.when: after the h100 install (engine 767a1bfc, seven gates pass; b300 25 cases identical) — full-GPU H100 500 cases
addenda.text: Ledgers $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sim-ledger6/hp-fg, comparison compare/ledger6 against compare/ledger5 (cold hold only) and compare/ledger4m (before both rules). Against ledger5: per-pc residency error 0.953 -> 0.932 (413 cases better, 44 worse); class attribution error 0.394 -> 0.389 in the mean (172 better, 283 worse); site residency error 0.285 -> 0.291 (164 better, 291 worse); imc_miss unchanged (-1.30 outside loops); code before the first anchor: outside loops -2.12 -> -2.53, inside loops -0.96 -> -1.58 points of residency. Against the state before both rules the site error is 0.296 -> 0.291 and the per-pc error 0.990 -> 0.932 (487 / 11). What happened: the engine no longer charges the readers of resident uniform constants (3.5 % of its residency before, which hardware has neither at the loads nor, on the probe, at the readers); the time removed sat on pcs where hardware waits for other reasons, so the per-pc match improves while the totals of those sites fall further below hardware. The deficit this uncovers is short_scoreboard: -1.84 points outside loops and -2.00 inside (before both rules +0.88 and -0.27). The rule is kept on the probe evidence (72 rows: a resident uniform line costs 0-7 cycles at the load and nothing at the readers); the site totals say where the next missing mechanism is, not that this one is wrong. Cycle error next to it: MAPE 8.62 % -> 9.78 % (7.87 % before both rules), P90 18.1 -> 19.5, median sim / hardware 0.937 -> 0.922, cases above 20 %: 29 -> 45.
